notes:
SIM FALLBACK — disclose in the build card and say it out loud on stage. FACTS.md says HARDWARE_PRESENT: no, so arm_io selects the simulator: nothing in this module has moved a servo, and no gesture was taught on a robot. All four trajectory JSONs carry source="sim-authored" plus a notes field saying so; task_demo is a hand-written slow tabletop pick-and-place, NOT a recorded demonstration. The arm's entire repertoire is that one trajectory.

Contract: `from arm import arm_io` with REPO_ROOT on sys.path -> home(speed=1.0), replay(traj_json_path, speed=1.0), gesture(name) for attention|decline|point_screen. Extras for F: arm_io.describe() returns the disclosure dict (backend, simulated, FACTS flag, cap, control_hz, gesture sources); arm_io.TASK_DEMO_PATH; arm_io.recover_home(). HARDWARE_PRESENT is read from FACTS.md at import through arm/facts.py — there is no constant in arm/ that can drift from it, and 'uncertain' resolves to not-present on purpose.

ORCHESTRATOR REDIRECT APPLIED: hardware branch is stubbed against the in-repo YAM driver (yam/arm.py YamArm), not lerobot/SO-101. yam is imported INSIDE hw_backend.connect(), never at module scope, so `import arm.arm_io` works with no python-can/gs_usb installed (smoke check [8] asserts this). arm/model.py mirrors yam.arm.ARM_JOINTS limits rad->deg and derives the velocity cap from yam.arm.SafetyLimits.max_step_per_tick (0.02 rad) at the driver's 100 Hz tick = 114.6 deg/s, capped at 30% = 34.4 deg/s; hw_backend.verify_against_yam() re-checks that mirror against the live module at connect time and refuses to run if it has drifted. HOME_POSE_DEG is scripts/plan_and_run.py's measured resting pose (joint2/joint3 clamped up to their 0.0 bound). Channel vector is 7 wide: joint1-joint6 in degrees plus a SIM-ONLY gripper in percent-open, because yam.arm.ARM_JOINTS deliberately excludes the gripper (uncalibrated jaw travel) — on hardware task_demo runs as a six-joint reach with the jaws untouched.

Safety, real code shared by both backends (not sim-only): motion.enforce_velocity_cap() slows any over-fast segment by TIME DILATION, never position clipping, and runs on every motion including home; motion.load_trajectory() rejects out-of-limit waypoints (SoftLimitError); KeyboardInterrupt during a motion calls backend hold() and latches a freeze — it does NOT home, and every further motion call raises ArmFrozen until arm_io.recover_home() gets an explicit 'h' keypress, which then homes at 25% speed. A non-interactive stdin counts as no consent. Smoke test exercises all of that (checks [5]-[7]).

NOT VERIFIED, needs a human before any hardware run (also listed in hw_backend.preflight_checklist()): self-collision. yam/arm.py records that ~10% of in-limit poses self-collide and that the driver does not check; mujoco is not installed and the i2rt URDF is not on this machine, so yam.environment.ArmSafetyChecker could not be run. Poses were authored conservatively instead — joint3 does the lifting, joint2 stays <=18 deg against a ~105 deg self-collision threshold, and smoke asserts a 45 deg ceiling. Second hardware hazard already written into the checklist: yam.arm's 0xD comms-lost latch needs a keep-alive stream between motions, and the demo waits on human keypresses between beats.

For F: sim runs in real time by default (ARM_SIM_REALTIME=1) so beats are timeable — attention 3.4s, decline 7.4s, point_screen 7.4s, task_demo 19.4s at speed=1.0 (39s at speed=0.5). Set ARM_SIM_REALTIME=0 to make it instant, ARM_SIM_RENDER=0 to skip the ~2s/motion gif render during the live demo (the stills in arm/sim_out/ are already rendered for the screen). Rendering during a beat is the only thing that will make the arm feel laggy.

For the orchestrator: arm/sim_out/ is 4.2 MB of regenerable gif/png. It is NOT gitignored and .gitignore is outside my write scope — decide whether to ignore it or commit the stills only before the repo goes public.
